title: Tim Cook Used His Last WWDC to Bet Everything on a New Siri. Apple Has Been Late Before.
excerpt: Siri AI, built on Google Gemini, can read your screen, recall old conversations, and run third-party agents. India's 100 million iPhone users are watching.
body:
Tim Cook walked onstage at Apple Park on Monday for what is almost certainly his final WWDC keynote as CEO, and he used it to unveil the most significant overhaul of Siri since the assistant launched in 2011. The new version, called Siri AI, is designed to close a gap with ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude that has widened embarrassingly over the past two years.

"Truly helpful AI must be centred around you and your needs," said Craig Federighi, Apple's software chief. "This means integrating AI deep into the products you use every day."

Cook, who announced his retirement earlier this year after 15 years as CEO, will hand the reins to hardware chief John Ternus in September. Monday's presentation carried the weight of a farewell — the architect of Apple's supply chain revolution and its $3.5 trillion market cap making one last case for the company's relevance in the AI era.

https://x.com/tim_cook/status/2063973568787226897

## What Siri AI Actually Does

The revamped assistant is built on Apple's second-generation Foundation Models, developed in collaboration with Google's Gemini technology — a partnership announced in January that immediately raised eyebrows across the industry.

Siri AI can now understand what is on a user's screen, pull information from the web, and perform actions across multiple apps in a single request. It can recall previous conversations, find information buried in Messages or Mail — a friend's address shared in passing, say — even if it was never formally saved. A dedicated Siri app syncs conversations via iCloud across iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, and Vision Pro.

Apple has also introduced an AI agent marketplace, allowing third-party developers to build agents that can book reservations, manage tasks, edit documents, or control smart home devices through Siri.

The company said it will launch a beta version later this year, though Siri AI will initially not be available in the EU or China due to regulatory requirements.

## Why It Matters for India

Apple's India story has been one of the most dramatic turnarounds in the company's history. India is now Apple's fastest-growing major market and one of its most important manufacturing hubs. The company has expanded production through partners Foxconn and Tata Electronics, with iPhone assembly in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka now accounting for a growing share of global output.

A smarter Siri matters for India because the current version has been notably weak in handling Indian languages, accents, and local context. Apple said the new Foundation Models offer "improved reasoning and understanding," but did not specifically address multilingual capabilities for Indian languages during the keynote.

For India's 100+ million iPhone users, the question is whether Siri AI will work meaningfully in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and other widely spoken languages — or remain primarily an English-language tool with bolted-on translations.

The developer ecosystem matters too. India has the second-largest pool of iOS developers after the U.S., and the new agent marketplace could open significant revenue opportunities for Indian startups building vertical AI tools — from healthcare bots to travel assistants.

## Cook's Legacy

Cook's final WWDC as CEO comes at an inflection point for the company. Under his leadership, Apple grew from a $350 billion company to the world's most valuable, driven by iPhone dominance, a services business that now generates over $100 billion annually, and a manufacturing strategy that turned India and Vietnam into critical supply chain nodes.

But on AI, Apple has been conspicuously behind. The original Apple Intelligence features, launched in 2024, were widely seen as underwhelming. Siri's overhaul was promised that year, then delayed repeatedly. Competitors moved aggressively — Google embedded Gemini across its ecosystem, Microsoft built Copilot into Windows and Office, and ChatGPT became the fastest-growing consumer app in history.

The question Cook is leaving for Ternus is whether Siri AI can be a genuine competitor or merely a late entrant in a race already defined by OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic. Apple's privacy-first approach — processing AI on-device where possible, using its Private Cloud Compute infrastructure for heavier tasks — is a genuine differentiator. But differentiation only matters if the product actually works.

Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management was measured: "They haven't done anything that really blows people away."

Monday's keynote suggests Apple knows it. Whether Siri AI is the answer — or another incremental step — will become clear when the beta ships later this year.

*Sources: Reuters, TechCrunch, CNN, Barron's, IANS*
